title: Women rate most men below average
finding: On OkCupid, women rated about 80% of men as worse-looking than medium. Men's ratings of women formed a symmetric curve.
source: OkCupid OkTrends, "Your Looks and Your Inbox" (Christian Rudder)
caveat: Company blog data from 2009, not peer reviewed

title: Messages pile up at the top
finding: Two-thirds of men's messages went to the best-looking third of women on the site.
source: OkCupid OkTrends, "Your Looks and Your Inbox"

title: Stated taste versus behaviour
finding: Men from 20 to 50 said women aged 20 to 23 were most attractive, yet mostly messaged women within a few years of their own age.
source: Christian Rudder, Dataclysm (OkCupid data), via Jezebel
caveat: Opinions on one site, not outcomes

title: Everyone messages up
finding: Men and women both pursued partners about 25% more desirable than themselves, and replies fell as the gap grew.
caveat: One free dating site, heterosexual users

title: Who matches the men
finding: In an experiment with 14 Tinder accounts, 86% of the matches the male profiles received came from other men; women's profiles gathered matches quickly.
source: Tyson et al., "A First Look at User Activity on Tinder" 2016

title: Online-begun marriages broke up slightly less
finding: Among 19,131 people married 2005–2012, more than one-third met online; break-ups were 5.96% versus 7.67% for offline couples.
caveat: Commissioned by eHarmony; the authors called the effects small

title: App couples want to move in sooner
finding: Swiss couples who met on dating apps had stronger plans to live together, the same relationship satisfaction, and were more often mixed in education and distance.

title: Same-race preference was strong
finding: On one US dating site, users showed strong same-race preferences, and women weighed income more heavily than looks.
source: Hitsch, Hortaçsu & Ariely, Quantitative Marketing and Economics 2010

title: Apps tie the office
finding: For Japanese couples married within a year in 2023, matching apps and work were tied as the top way to meet.
source: Meiji Yasuda Life survey, via Manila Times

title: One country, two marriage cultures
finding: Women who chose their own husband: 96% in Manipur, under 1% in Rajasthan.
source: India Human Development Survey 2011–12, via The Quint

title: Most app users feel burnt out
finding: 78% of US dating-app users said they feel burnout at least sometimes; 80% of women and 74% of men.

title: Men like it more than women
finding: 57% of men who dated online called it positive; women were split, 48% positive and 51% negative.

title: Marriage lost its shine in Korea
finding: About one in three South Koreans aged 19–34 felt positive about marrying in 2022, down from 56.5% in 2012.

title: First UK drop in app use
finding: The UK's top four dating apps lost users between 2023 and 2024; Tinder alone lost about 600,000.
caveat: Total adults visiting dating services was broadly flat
